description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy of six different methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME) relative to varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and utilizes a logarithmic scale, featuring labeled ticks at 0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and employs a linear scale with values ranging from 60 to a grid line above 80, with tick marks spaced at intervals of 5. Six individual solid lines, each with distinct markers, plot data at four corresponding positions along the x-axis, all displaying a steady upward trend. The "Base" line is black with circle markers, demonstrating an increase from approximately 64 at the first data point to 71 at the final point. The "FT" line is blue with downward-pointing triangle markers, rising from roughly 65 to 73 across the x-axis. The "IKE" line is red with upward-pointing triangle markers, climbing from about 67.5 to 75.5. The "MEMIT" line is purple with pentagon markers, starting around 69.5 and growing to approximately 78. The "MEND" line is brown with diamond markers, increasing from an initial value of approximately 71 to end near 80.5. Finally, the "ROME" line is green with square markers, beginning at approximately 74.5 and following a continuous upward path to reach approximately 84 at the end of the plotted range.
